senses.definition: Used after a verb to say that there has never been an occasion to do something.
Used after a potential verb to say that there is nothing one cannot do; to say that something is possible.

examples.sentence: 吾輩が鼠をとったことはないと言うと、黒は、人間が猫のとった鼠を取り上げて交番へ持って行き、五銭をもらうという話をした。
examples.gloss: have never done; there has been no occasion to

examples.sentence: こんなに寝ていても仕事が続くなら、猫にだって出来ないことはない、と。
examples.gloss: there is no matter that; nothing is such that

previous.explanation_en: After a verb in the た-form, こと makes the action into an event or experience, and ない denies that it occurred. は marks that event as the point being discussed, so the construction says there has been no occasion when the action happened: the speaker has never done it.

parts.contribution_en: Turns the preceding verb phrase into an event or experience that can be discussed.
Marks that event or experience as the point being discussed.
Denies that the event or experience occurred.
